title: Balanced Brackets
parentTitle: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
twist: Builds on Runes on the Castle Door: every position offers the same two brackets, but which one may come next depends on the whole prefix so far: how many brackets are used and how many are still open.
statement:
You are given two whole numbers, `n` and `maxDepth`.

Return **every** string made of exactly `n` opening brackets `(` and `n` closing brackets `)` that is **balanced** and never more than `maxDepth` deep.

A string is **balanced** when, reading from left to right, the number of `)` never exceeds the number of `(` so far. The **depth** at any point is the number of `(` so far minus the number of `)` so far: how many brackets are open at once. The depth must never be more than `maxDepth`.

You may return the strings in any order.

examples.explanation: These are the balanced strings with three pairs that never have more than 2 brackets open. `((()))` is left out: after its third `(`, 3 brackets are open at once.
A string with three `(` can never have more than 3 brackets open, so maxDepth rules nothing out. All five balanced strings count.
With maxDepth 1, each `(` must close before the next one opens, so only one string is left.
